title: Full AES-256 differential distinguisher conditional on a weak related-key pair, BKN 2009

target.description: Standard full 14-round AES-256 with its actual key schedule, using the related-key differential of Section 4.1 and Appendix A.

setting.reference_model: Editorial statement of the differential test: compare the selected pair of AES-256 permutations with two independent uniform 128-bit permutations, using plaintext pairs at the fixed input difference and testing the specified output difference. No numerical overall distinguishing advantage is asserted.
setting.key_relation: A fixed XOR master-key difference: K and K XOR DeltaK. DeltaK is fixed by the subkeys K^0 and K^1 in Appendix A, pp.247-248; applicability additionally requires the five active key-schedule S-box transitions of the trail.
setting.key_population: Conditional on a weak related-key pair satisfying the key-schedule trail; the authors estimate one qualifying pair among 2^35 related-key pairs on average.
setting.plaintext_model: Chosen plaintext pairs at the fixed difference DeltaP in Appendix A's related-key distinguisher trail.
assumptions: The two secret related-key encryption oracles are already available and their pair satisfies the weak key-schedule condition.
The data-path trail probability 2^-119 is an author estimate conditional on that weak pair.
The cost of finding a weak pair in a larger pool is excluded from this conditional record.

time.note: Abstract p.231 and discussion p.233 give 2^120 time and data for a qualifying pair. This is not the cost of scanning 2^35 candidate pairs.

data.note: The stated 2^120 total corresponds to testing approximately 2^119 chosen plaintext pairs, with one encryption under each of the two related keys. Table 1's 2^119 per-key entry is consistent with this total.

memory.note: The abstract and p.233 explicitly describe negligible memory; no byte or block count is assigned.

preprocessing.note: No separately reusable preprocessing budget is reported for the conditional distinguisher.

success.description: No finite-budget distinguishing decision probability or advantage is quantified. The state-trail2^-119 and key-population incidence2^-35 have separate conditioning. Neither the2^120 data budget nor an expected number of right pairs defines a decision probability without its test distribution. No pool-hit model is added.

components.description: Section4.1: five key-schedule transitions each2^-7 give mean weak-pair incidence2^-35 in the source key model. This is not the probability that a2^35-pair pool contains a qualifying pair; independence between tested pairs is not established.
Section4.1: source state trail probability2^(-14*6-5*7), conditional on the five schedule transitions. It is not a finite-budget distinguishing decision success or advantage.

review.scope: Exact-edition endpoint-specific success audit. Local pair filters, conditional trails, weak-pair incidence and expected counts keep their own experiment; correlation is not a decision probability. Existing conflicts, resources, targets, settings and full-audit gates remain unchanged.

evidence.locator: Printed p.231 abstract; p.233 Table 1 and discussion; Section 4.1 p.242; Appendix A pp.247-249.
evidence.interpretation: Section 4.1 explicitly separates the 19 active data-path S-boxes from five active key-schedule S-boxes. Their probabilities give the conditional trail and weak-pair fraction, respectively. The selected record is the secret-key related-key test, not the paper's chosen-key multicollision construction.

evidence.locator: CRYPTO proceedings PDF12–14 / printed242–244 Sections4.1–4.2 and Figure4; PDF3 Table1 distinguishes weak-pair and pool costs.
evidence.interpretation: No finite-budget distinguishing decision probability or advantage is quantified. The state-trail2^-119 and key-population incidence2^-35 have separate conditioning. Neither the2^120 data budget nor an expected number of right pairs defines a decision probability without its test distribution. No pool-hit model is added.

limitations: Not an all-key attack using two related keys; weak-pair selection is an explicit precondition.
The stated work and probability analysis have not been independently reproduced.
The source's chosen-key q-multicollisions and Davies-Meyer pseudo-collisions are different target experiments and are not represented by this record.
